_notes: Locally added -- upstream pinmame-nvram-maps has no map for Big Buck Hunter Pro.
Built from a 4-player game driven through the cabinet's own streamer; the addresses came from
watching how bytes behaved during play rather than from reading values off a display.
current_player and current_ball are adjacent in CPU RAM at 0x00031FCC and 0x00031FCD, player low
and ball high. Two other adjacent pairs also counted, at 0x02111A04 and 0x02111A0C, but both sit
in NVRAM with the player byte ABOVE the ball -- the reverse of the eight SAM games already
measured -- so they are rejected. Without that rule this ROM had three candidates and no way to
choose between them.
Scores are 4 bytes on 8-byte centres from 0x021109E4, the only group of four evenly spaced values
rising monotonically through the game.
High score records are 0x20 apart from 0x02102AB8, bounded by where the 16-bit checksum stops
validating: six records pass, the seventh does not. The first five hold Stern's factory ladder.
The sixth is the Open Season Champion, read off the machine's DMD after game over -- 'LON' at
50,000,000, which is what the record decodes to.
Only bbh_170 is claimed; SAM addresses move between revisions.
Confirmed after the table exited: the map decodes that game as 4 players scoring 952,010 /
game_over, tilted and credits come from an 803-frame recording of live memory spanning an
operator-menu session and a full game with a tilt on ball 1. The session also promoted
indices 30 and 32 as the free_play-relative rule predicted.
0x00031FFE is the status bitfield trn_174h, avr_200, avs_170 and bdk_294 keep at ball+0x31, in
trn_174h's exact encoding: 1 in attract, 19 in play, 21 for the eight samples between the tilt
and the end of the tilted ball, during which player 1's score sat frozen at 44,040. game_over
(mask 0x12, inverted) is correct in all 803 frames; tilted is bit 0x04.
credits at 0x0211100C, the eighth SAM game at that address. It read 9 -- the Maximum Credits
just set, so the credit count was capped -- and fell to 8 at game start.
